verses.text: Ephraim feeds on the wind. He chases the hot east wind all day long. He keeps telling more lies and doing more violence. He makes a treaty with Assyria and sends olive oil to Egypt.
The LORD also has a charge to bring against Judah. He will punish Jacob for his ways and pay him back for what he has done.
Even before he was born, Jacob grabbed his brother's heel. As a man, he struggled with God.
He struggled with the angel and won. He wept and begged for his blessing. He met God at Bethel, and there God spoke with us,
the LORD God of Armies. The LORD is his name!
So you must return to your God. Hold on to faithful love and justice, and always wait for your God.
The merchants use dishonest scales. They love to cheat.
Ephraim says, "I am very rich! I have become wealthy. With all my wealth, no one will find me guilty of any wrong or sin."
"But I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt. I will make you live in tents again, as you do at your appointed festival.
I spoke to the prophets and gave them many visions. Through the prophets I spoke in picture language."
Gilead is full of evil. Its people are worthless. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls. Their altars will become piles of stones in a plowed field.
Jacob ran away to the land of Aram. Israel worked to earn a wife. To pay for her, he took care of sheep.
Through a prophet the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt, and through a prophet he took care of them.
But Ephraim has made the LORD bitterly angry. So his Lord will leave him guilty of the blood he has shed and pay him back for his insults.
